Run manifest, health and boundary
`/app/run.json` installs, builds and serves the app on the published port, `/api/health` answers as published in Deployment, and the rules in Server boundary hold.

Accounts and sign-in
Local username and password accounts use the `spoor_session` cookie, the sign-in rate limit and a landing on `/explore` after sign-in or sign-up, as qualified in Business rules.

Grading routes and live settle signal
With `SPOOR_GRADING=1` the grading routes seed data, sign in, set the server clock, run checks, run lifecycle steps and switch storage as published, and every page shows `data-seq` and `data-pending` and applies live messages from `GET /api/events`.

One error shape and order
Every API error uses the one published body and code list and is decided in the one published order.

Drafted console look
The console carries the published visual design: a warm paper ground, one deep green accent, mono data and numerals with Inter interface text, outlined cards, and every named console component in its published place.

Built-in index and secrets from env
The term index, text analysis and scoring are written in the app's own source with no search engine or search library, and every service credential is read from the environment and never reaches the browser.

Query bar suggestions
`combobox "Query"` follows the published combobox keys and suggests field names, operators and values by cursor position, from the current space only.

Virtual events grid
`grid "Events"` keeps at most 60 rows in the page, publishes its row count, row indexes and row labels, sorts in the published order, and follows the published grid keys, column resizing and Tab exit.

Document panel and surrounding events
Opening an event shows `region "Document"` with the `panel-in` animation and focus on its close button, closing returns focus to the same row, and surrounding events list the published 5 before and 5 after.

Explore triage journey
An on-call engineer searches, works filter pills, moves between Explore regions with F6 and Tab, and hears the published result count after every search.

Time range and viewer zone
`dialog "Time range"` sets quick, relative and absolute ranges in the viewer's time zone with server time as now, and every displayed time uses the published format.

Histogram buckets across daylight saving
The histogram picks the published interval and aligns buckets in the viewer's zone, including the published 23-hour and 25-hour days.

Bucket Brush
Dragging over `group "Histogram"`, or Shift+arrows then Enter, sets the range to the selected buckets' outer edges, each changed bar runs `bar-settle`, and reduced motion shows final heights with no animation.

Range-following statistics journey
After a Bucket Brush change, the event count, field statistics, filter pills and grid follow the new range with no query text, and the published range announcement is made.

Alert rules and group windows
A structured alert rule measures each group over the published window, which never starts before the group's last change to active or recovered, so no event counts toward two state changes.

Group states and flapping
Each group moves through inactive, pending, active and recovered by the published transitions, keeps its state on a failed check, and is marked flapping with its actions held, as published.

Snoozes and maintenance windows
Snoozes and weekly maintenance windows in an IANA time zone hold actions on the server clock, and the first check after a window ends fires the published single action.

Live alert journey
In two browsers, a service owner and an on-call engineer see group states, overlays and the inbox change in place, acknowledge items and hear each state change announcement.

Published breakpoints and sheets
Phone, tablet and desk layouts change exactly at 768 and 1100 pixels with no horizontal page scroll at 360 pixels, and on a phone the time range and filters dialogs open as bottom sheets with `sheet-rise`.

Swipe to acknowledge
On a phone, swiping a group card left past 80 pixels with under 40 pixels of vertical travel acknowledges the group, and a shorter swipe springs back and changes nothing.

Cases
Cases move through open, investigating, resolved and closed by the published steps, collect groups, inbox items and traces, and the recent cases row shows the 3 newest.

Phone triage journey
At 360 pixels wide, an on-call engineer triages from alert cards, acknowledges by swipe, sets a range in the sheet, adds a group to a case and taps through spans, while a desk browser sees each change live.

Spoor Query syntax
Spoor Query matches fields, phrases, existence, ranges, relative dates, wildcards, grouped values, object scopes and escapes with NOT, AND and OR precedence and the published multi-value range rule.

Query errors at their position
Each malformed query answers 422 with the published sentence and 1-based position, shown in `alert "Query error"` with the caret moved to that position.

Query limits and work budget
Queries over the length, nesting or work limit, or past the result window, get the published refusal within the time budget while uploads keep being answered.

Text analysis
The three published analyzers give the published tokens, positions and offsets, shown in `table "Tokens"` on the analyze page.

Published scoring and explanation
Every result's score follows the published formula and rounding, and `tree "Score explanation"` and the explain JSON list parts that add up exactly to the score.

Phrases and highlights
Phrases match by position with stopwords holding their slot, and matched tokens are highlighted at their published offsets.

Pipeline processors
The six published processors, their single condition form and the one failure handler change, drop or refuse each event exactly as published.

Pipeline simulation
The simulate page shows each processor's result for every sample event, marks changed fields, and stores nothing.

Editing a pipeline in use
Saving a pipeline raises its version by one and affects only events stored afterwards.

Rollover and phases on the server clock
Lifecycle steps roll over the write generation once and move each generation forward to the furthest phase its age allows, measured from rollover on the server clock, as shown in the generation timeline.

Read-only generations
An edit to an event in a warm or archived generation answers 409 with the published text before any check of its body.

Archive confirmed by storage
A generation becomes archived only after storage confirms its segment object, searches read it back, and during a storage outage searches return the rest with the published partial results banner and skipped count.

Snapshot paging
A snapshot freezes one result list, and its pages never repeat or skip an event while others upload or roll over.

Snapshot expiry
A snapshot left unused for the published time on the server clock answers 410, and the grid shows the published expiry text with a way to start a new search.

Live tail
The live tail follows new events, pauses with a counted buffer of the published size, discards the oldest events past it, resumes, and shows the published rate limit text.

Bulk upload line results
Each newline-delimited line gets its own created, duplicate, dropped or failed result with the published line errors, a client `_id` never makes a second event, and type conflicts across generations are reported as published.

File uploads
A file of the wrong kind or over the size limit is refused before anything is stored; otherwise the file is kept in storage byte for byte before parsing, with live progress in every browser in the space.

Spoor Pipe commands
Spoor Pipe runs the six published commands with typed columns, the published rounding and the published sort tie-break.

Pipe errors
A malformed pipe shows the published sentence in `alert "Pipe error"`.

Trace view
The trace tree orders spans, places orphans, corrects clock skew, and shows self time, critical path and latency percentiles exactly as published.

Error budgets and burn rates
Each objective shows budget remaining, long and short burn rates and a status by the published formulas on the server clock.

Scoped API keys
A key is shown once, stored only as a hash, and gets the published 401, 404 and 403 refusals for expiry, revocation, other spaces and scope.

Space isolation and saved search copy
No surface shows another space's data, and a saved search copied into another space lands with its missing references reported as published.
/app/run.json holds exactly the string keys install, build and serve plus "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and those commands alone install, build and serve the app.
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree, as npm ls --omit=dev --all --json reports it) and the two bundled font families, each with its licence.

Every shipped package and font uses MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, BlueOak-1.0.0 or (fonts only) OFL-1.1, and none is AGPL, GPL, SSPL, BUSL or another source-available licence.
The app uses only Postgres and MinIO as backing services, and no shipped package is a search engine, full-text index or search ranking library.
The app loads no font, script or style from outside its own origin and registers no service worker.
The provided service configuration and the environment variable names it sets are left unchanged.
package-lock.json is committed, and all backend and frontend source is TypeScript.
